This does not seem like an appropriate name for this file. Is this even an “entity”?  At least make it related to your system name?
Done

This doesn't look done "huygens_spdm_responder.json" is the current name, and that's not an "entity".  SPDM is one property of many of an entity, the entity (card, board, whatever) needs a name that's distinct from the protocols it supports.
Changed the file name to `huygens_attestable_peer_bmc.json`

huygens_attestable_peer_bmc still isn't a name.  what is it you're talking to?  Is it a board with only a BMC on it?  "atttestable" is a property of the device (ie an exposes record) not the name of the device itself.

Maybe Huygens_bmc.json is what you want?
s

If there are two reponders, How the object looks like.

/xyz/openbmc_project/SpdmTcpResponder/<objectID>

/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Huygens_Bmc_Peer/SpdmTcpResponder_1
/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Huygens_Bmc_Peer/SpdmTcpResponder_2
If the hostname is empty what will be the object ID?

"Name" property is used to create the object path for the exposes record.

Based on this configuration EM hosts below object path
/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Huygens_Bmc_Peer/SpdmTcpResponder_1
what happens if you find matching LLDP object with empty ManagementAddressIPv4 address which is possible if tcp endpoint has only Ipv6 address.
This configuration looks for only IPv4 address. When the ManagementAddressIPv4 property is empty, Entity Manager will create the SpdmTcpResponder object with an empty value for the Hostname property

> If the hostname is empty what will be the object ID?

Does this matter?
Since the Name is used as the last segment of the D-Bus path, it does not make sense in this context.

please wrap this at 72 characters each line.

Adding IPv6 support will require schema modifications, which will be addressed in a subsequent commit. The internal Ethernet interface currently uses an IPv4 address in IBM System.

LLDP advertises both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. by default ipv6 enabled on most of IPv6 supported system including BMC(eth0 & eth1). IPv6 Address support needed.
i think this file changes could be in a different standalone patch
Acknowledged

The changes looks good to me, I see that https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/83533 is close to merge. @archana.kakani@ibm.com - where is the code that implements the TLV interface ? That info is missing. I think we want that also to be merged before we can get this in ? right ?
I have added the commit details for the code implementing TLV interface in the commit message. As mentioned by Matt, we will just wait till the PDI gets merged for this.
prefer: BMC
Done
The name is not the type.  The name should describe WHAT in the system is responding.
Yes, This could be BMC, Satelite BMC or Redundant BMC in this context.
Done
Right, so pick a name for what it is in THIS system.
This scares me a bit.  Do we really want LLDP in this probe?  This seems like something we could just encapsulate entirely within the application?

As per the design document https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/redfish-spdm-attestation.md,
`For SPDM-over-TCP, SPDM daemon can query entity-manager for information about remote TCP endpoints, including the hostname / ip-address & port details from the SpdmTcpResponder interface `.

IBM Huygens is the system with redundant BMC support. The peer BMC is discovered via ethernet protocol LLDP. The SPDM daemon uses the SPDM TCP Responder configuration interface to identify SPDM-capable devices and perform attestation.

That quoted statement mentions nothing about the probe.  I was assuming we'd use the normal probe statements and not add an arbitrary network protocol here, same as we did for sattelite.  Is this really the only way on a Huygens system to know if there's a BMC?  BMC has no fru and is only detectable based on LLDP being up and working?

Hi Ed

I remember we have already discussed on this topic sometime back over discord,
LLDP is neighbor discovery protocol, The network neighbor represents a piece of hardware. since SPDM is trying to identify TCP endpoints devices, it needs to probe LLDP interfaces
